decisions.reason: The distributed ALCMS control unit sits at the core of the firm's airfield lighting expertise, so the firm can interpret its results and improve it through its own R&D, which makes it a long-lived infrastructure product worth keeping.

The air situation display builds on the firm's tower and surveillance integration know-how and complements its MLAT and collaboration offerings, so keeping it supports its integrated-operations strategy.
Training on its own airport systems draws directly on knowledge the firm already holds, costs little to sustain and strengthens customer ties, so it is likely to be kept.
The airfield ground lighting course is closely tied to the firm's core lighting business and its service model, though as a narrow course it could be folded into broader training offerings.

The collaboration software fits the firm's move toward data-driven collaborative decision-making, but software evolves quickly and may be rebranded or merged into a platform, which adds some risk of withdrawal.
The MLAT system is a flagship that extends the firm's surveillance knowledge and is supported by its in-house R&D, so the firm will keep developing it rather than drop it.
